topic: Music and Dance Gharanas: Kathak, Lucknow and Benares Gharanas
description: The Gharana system forms a crucial part of the music and dance traditions of Uttar Pradesh. Specifically, Kathak, the Lucknow Gharana, and the Benares Gharana are highly significant for the state's cultural history and are frequently tested in competitive exams.

sections.title: Gharana System and Kathak
sections.description: Fundamental concepts regarding the Gharana tradition and the major classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh.

key_concepts.explanation: A specific musical or dance style that is passed down from generation to generation through a strict lineage or the traditional Guru-Shishya (teacher-disciple) tradition.
The primary classical dance of Uttar Pradesh, originating from ancient 'Katha-kars' (storytellers). It is a unique blend of Radha-Krishna legends and the cultural influence of Mughal courts.
A semi-classical singing style that is deeply associated with Kathak dance performances, primarily developed and nurtured in Lucknow and Benares.

sections.title: Lucknow Gharana
sections.description: Developed in the City of Nawabs, this Gharana is globally renowned for its elegance, grace, and emphasis on expression (Abhinaya).

historical_events.event: Patronage of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah
historical_events.significance: Marked the Golden Era of Kathak and Thumri in Awadh, which firmly established the foundation of the Lucknow Gharana.

key_associations.extra_info: India's most renowned Kathak dancer and choreographer, honored with the Padma Vibhushan.
One of the founding pillars of the Lucknow Gharana, famous for composing excellent Thumri pieces tailored for Kathak.
Widely revered as 'Mallika-e-Ghazal' (Queen of Ghazals), she was deeply associated with the musical heritage of Lucknow.

sections.title: Benares Gharana
sections.description: Developed in the holy city of Kashi, this Gharana emphasizes devotion, powerful rhythmic complexity (Tandava), and intricate spins (Chakkars).

key_associations.extra_info: A world-famous Tabla maestro who belonged to the Benares Gharana.
Revered as the 'Queen of Thumri', she was a legendary classical singer who brought international recognition to the Benares Gharana.
A Bharat Ratna awardee whose life and music were deeply connected to Benares and the Baba Vishwanath Temple.

sections.title: Other Major Musical Gharanas of Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: Besides Lucknow and Benares, other prominent Khyal and Dhrupad gharanas that evolved in various regions of Uttar Pradesh.

key_associations.extra_info: Founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan. Bharat Ratna Pt. Bhimsen Joshi was the most famous vocalist of this gharana.
Popularized by Ustad Faiyaz Khan, who was widely known for his powerful, deep voice and rhythmic control.
Stylistically closely related to the Gwalior Gharana; the legendary Ustad Rashid Khan belonged to this musical lineage.
This gharana is primarily known for preserving the ancient Dhrupad singing tradition.

sections.title: Important Facts and Institutes
sections.description: Crucial exam-oriented one-liner facts and prominent cultural institutions related to Kathak and the Gharanas of Uttar Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: Kathak is the only classical dance originating from Uttar Pradesh and is recognized among the eight major classical dances of India.
The Lucknow Gharana of Kathak places heavy emphasis on elegance, grace, and acting (Abhinaya), whereas the Benares Gharana focuses on the Tandava aspect and pure rhythm.
The National Institute of Kathak (Rashtriya Kathak Sansthan) is headquartered in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
To promote and develop the state's music and drama, the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in Lucknow in the year 1963.
